one_liner: Senior Executive Service job leading ACF's entire grants management office: grants policy, oversight of risk and audit resolution, grants systems, and the staff who run them.
fit_summary: This is an SES role that requires executive-level leadership of a large, complex federal grants portfolio and organization. Daniel's IEM consulting work and policy knowledge are relevant context, especially if it touched FEMA or disaster-recovery grants, but nothing on file shows executive leadership of a grants organization. The Executive Resources Board will likely screen Daniel out unless that IEM role involved senior management of grants programs and staff.
eligibility: Open to the public, so federal status is not required, but this is a Senior Executive Service career appointment.
Your two-page resume must show all five Executive Core Qualifications and all three Technical Qualifications. Separate narratives are not accepted.
TQ 1-3 require demonstrated executive-level experience in federal grants management policy, grants operations and organizational leadership, and principal advisory and stakeholder work.
If selected, your qualifications must be certified by OPM's SES Qualifications Review Board, and you then serve a one-year probationary period.
No education requirement and no clearance required.
strategy: Before investing time, decide honestly whether your IEM role included supervising staff and owning grants-related outcomes such as FEMA Public Assistance or HMGP administration, compliance, or closeout. If not, treat this as a long shot and target GS-11 to GS-13 grants management specialist or emergency-management program roles instead.
If you apply, map every bullet to a named TQ or ECQ and use the posting's exact language (risk-based, internal controls, audit resolution, driving efficiency) within the two-page limit.
Frame the consulting work as delivered outcomes for government clients: the portfolio dollar value, team size led, process improvements, and audit or compliance findings resolved.
Use your policy and relationship strengths as evidence for TQ 3 and ECQ 1: advising senior officials and representing positions to federal, state, and local stakeholders.
For each job, list dates, hours per week, and a title that accurately reflects your level.
Apply between October 20 and November 3, 2026, and do not wait for the final day.
resume_bullets: Led [number]-person team supporting [client agency]'s administration of $[amount] in [FEMA PA/HMGP/other] grants, applying risk-based reviews that [result] by [metric].
Advised [title of senior official] on [grants compliance/recovery policy issue], developing corrective actions that resolved [number] audit findings by [date].
Redesigned [grants process or system] for [client], cutting processing time from [X] to [Y] days and [specific efficiency outcome].
interview_questions: Describe how you led a large grants organization through significant change, and how you held people accountable.
How have you applied risk-based approaches and internal controls to prevent improper payments or waste?
Walk us through an audit resolution or corrective action plan you oversaw from finding to closure.
How would you advise ACF leadership on a proposed regulation that affects grantees nationwide?
watch_outs: SES positions almost always require years of senior leadership. Without clear executive-level grants experience, you will likely be rated ineligible.
Anything beyond page 2 of your resume will not be reviewed, and an over-length resume may be disqualified.
Even after selection, OPM QRB certification is required, followed by a one-year probationary period.
The job is located in Washington, DC with telework but is not remote, so expect a commute from Manassas.
